name: transfer-list
purpose: Dual-list transfer control: a labelled **source** listbox and a labelled **target** listbox with a control column to move items between them. Use it when the consumer needs to build a subset from a pool of options where both the chosen set and the remaining pool stay visible. Named after the MUI Transfer List (Ant Design calls it Transfer; it was PickList before 6.0), derived from the PrimeVue PickList behavior but rewritten to our conventions (no Figma); the visual surface is a best-effort first draft to validate. Compound, composition API: the root (`<TransferList>`) owns the bound data (`v-model` = `[sourceItems, targetItems]`) and the shared selection/move state, and provides it through `provide`/`inject`. The consumer composes the anatomy — `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, `<TransferList.Target>` — and the context-aware `<TransferList.Controls>` wires the move buttons with no props. Each list is data-driven: items come from the root's bound pair and render through the list's `#item` slot (repeated data stays as props, not hand-authored rows). Double-clicking an option moves it to the opposite list (emitting `item-double-click`); this auto-move can be turned off with `move-on-double-click`. The two lists sit side by side on wider viewports and stack vertically (with the controls as a horizontal row between them) on narrow ones; the move arrows point left/right side-by-side and up/down when stacked.
useWhen: Use TransferList only when the person builds a large subset and must see the chosen and remaining items side by side. To pick several values in a compact form field use MultiSelect; for two to five options use a Checkbox per option.
Building a subset from a pool where both the chosen and the remaining items stay visible (domains assigned to an application, members of a team).
Moving many items at once with move-all and multi-selection.
Lists that load separately, each with its own `loading` state.
avoidWhen: Picking a few values in a compact field → use `multi-select`.
Selecting rows of tabular data with columns, sorting, or pagination → use `table` with row selection.
A handful of fixed options → use a horizontal `field` with a `checkbox` for each.
related: multi-select` — compact dropdown for multi-pick when the remaining pool does not need to stay visible.
table` — row selection over tabular data.
checkbox` — independent boolean or small-set multi-pick.
bestPractices: Set `track-by` to a unique item field so rows keep stable keys across moves and the selection follows the record when the lists change; without it rows and the selection are keyed by their index.
Set `title` on both `TransferList.Source` and `TransferList.Target`; it is the listbox's accessible name.
Listen to `move` for side effects such as saving the assignment instead of diffing `v-model`.
Set `:move-on-double-click="false"` when double-click should do something else; `item-double-click` still fires.

props.name: trackBy
props.doc: Item field that identifies a record, the same name as `card-list`: each row's render key and the key of the selection, so an external change to the v-model pair keeps the selection on its records. Empty falls back to the index.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables all selection and move controls and applies disabled tokens.

props.name: moveOnDoubleClick
props.doc: When true, double-clicking an item moves it to the opposite list. Set false to keep `item-double-click` firing without the move.

events.name: move
events.notes: Fired after items move between lists, with the moved items.

events.name: item-double-click
events.payload: (event: MouseEvent, payload: { list: 'source' | 'target'; item: unknown; index: number })
events.notes: Fired when an option is double-clicked. `event` is the dblclick; `payload` carries the item, its index, and which list it was in. Fires regardless of `moveOnDoubleClick`, but not while the component is disabled or a list is loading.

slots.name: default
slots.scope: { move, moveAll, hasSelection, count, disabled, loading }
slots.notes: Composition slot; receives `<TransferList.Source>`, `<TransferList.Controls>`, and `<TransferList.Target>` in flow order. The scope exposes the move actions plus selection/loading state, so a consumer can render custom controls inside the root in place of `<TransferList.Controls>`.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import TransferList from '@aziontech/webkit/transfer-list'
  import { ref } from 'vue'

  const model = ref([
    [
      { id: 1, label: 'Edge Functions' },
      { id: 2, label: 'WAF' },
      { id: 3, label: 'Image Processor' }
    ],
    [{ id: 4, label: 'Cache' }]
  ])
</script>

<template>
  <TransferList
    v-model="model"
    track-by="id"
  >
    <TransferList.Source title="Available">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </TransferList.Source>

    <TransferList.Controls />

    <TransferList.Target title="Selected">
      <template #item="{ item }">{{ item.label }}</template>
    </TransferList.Target>
  </TransferList>
</template>
